clue.text: Fool, silly chap in one type of headgear

parts.note: a clot is a slang word for a stupid person

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters of the word chap are thrown into a foolish disorder

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a daft man wearing a particular kind of hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool' looks like the definition but is wordplay; the headgear is a flat working man's cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat cap of woollen material, associated with working-class northern England, is a kind of hat.

clue.text: Watch diving bird getting submerged all right

indicators.note: the bird is plunged around the other piece, so the word for all right sits inside it

parts.note: the loon is the North American name for the diver, a water bird that dives for fish
OK is the informal word for all right

explanation.surface: An observer watches a water bird dive under and come up fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting submerged' has the bird take the other piece under water, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To look on is to watch as a spectator without taking part.

clue.text: Bone, black one buried in small island to the north

indicators.note: buried in signals the black-one pair goes inside the other piece
in a down clue, heading north means the word for small island is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: an ait (or eyot) is a small island in a river
B is the pencil-grading abbreviation for black
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A black bone is unearthed on a small island up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the north' reverses AIT to TIA; 'buried in' places B and I inside it: TI-BI-A.
explanation.definitionFit: The tibia is the shinbone, the larger of the two bones of the lower leg.

clue.text: State prisoner getting delivery, about to break free

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: the abbreviation for about escapes from the word for delivery, so it is dropped

parts.note: diction is a speaker's manner of delivery
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A state prisoner is being handed over, about to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' suggests handing over, but it is a speaker's manner of speech; 'to break free' lets the about-letter escape.
explanation.definitionFit: A condition is a state of being, as in 'in good condition'.

clue.text: Fish in river with member, getting a number

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A fish swims in a river beside a politician who gets a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The pompano is a food fish of warm Atlantic waters, related to jacks.

clue.text: Game defender to move towards his own goalkeeper?

parts.note: go is the Japanese board game of territory
a back is a defending player in football

explanation.surface: A defender is asked to drop deep towards his own keeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game defender' reads as one football phrase but is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat is to return, and a defender doing that heads towards his own keeper.

clue.text: Maybe oxygen starts to prevent such?

definitions.text: Maybe oxygen starts to prevent such?

parts.note: oxygen is one example of a gas, hence 'maybe'

indicators.note: starts asks for the opening letters of the words prevent and such

explanation.surface: Breathing oxygen might stop someone from struggling for air.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: breathing oxygen stops sharp intakes of breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp short breaths are what an oxygen supply could stop in someone short of air.

clue.text: Innocent and weak, restricted by sanction

indicators.note: restricted by means held within the word for sanction

parts.note: to bless is to approve or sanction
a lame excuse is a weak one

explanation.surface: Someone innocent and feeble is penalised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sanction' reads as a penalty but here means approve; 'restricted by' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without fault deserves no censure, so innocent and free from guilt are synonyms.

clue.text: Certain office workers less productive in Civil Service

indicators.note: in places the word for less productive within the abbreviation

parts.note: a leaner year is a less productive one

explanation.surface: Some civil servants are getting less done.
explanation.definitionFit: Office cleaners are workers employed in offices, after hours, so they are one kind of office staff.

clue.text: Sweet request to note blessing all around

indicators.note: the word for blessing is placed all around the abbreviation

parts.note: a boon is a blessing or benefit
NB, nota bene, is Latin for note well

explanation.surface: A sweet note asks everyone to pass round good wishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'request to note' is the Latin nota bene; 'all around' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonbon is a small sugary confection, a candy or chocolate.

clue.text: Doctors in service taking a long time

parts.note: a Mass is a church service
ages means a long time

explanation.surface: Physicians attending church stay for an age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctors' is a verb here: to doctor figures is to falsify them.
explanation.definitionFit: To massage data or figures is to falsify or manipulate them, the same as doctoring.

clue.text: Boy with a time at home given a piece to play

parts.note: a son is a boy
in means at home

explanation.surface: A boy at home with time on his hands is handed something to play.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, simple sonata is a musical composition to be performed, a piece for playing.

clue.text: Noticing headless insect in grass

indicators.note: in puts the shortened insect within the word for grass

parts.note: to grass is to inform on someone; to sing is the same slang

indicators.note: headless removes the first letter from the insect word

parts.note: a bee is an insect

explanation.surface: Someone spots a decapitated bug lying in the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' looks like a lawn but is the informer's verb. 'headless' cuts BEE to EE, which goes 'in' SING.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing something is observing or spotting it, which is what noticing means.

clue.text: More trying to set out some mathematics

indicators.note: set out means arranged afresh, so the letters of the opening three words are laid out anew

explanation.surface: Trying harder to lay out some sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Trigonometry is the branch of maths dealing with angles and sides of triangles.

clue.text: It's certainly not new, what some clocks have

definitions.meaning: second-hand twice over, i.e. used by previous owners
the hand showing seconds is the third on a clock face after hour and minute

explanation.definitionFit: Goods passed through more than one previous owner are far from new; and clocks with a seconds hand have a third pointer.

clue.text: Female involved in a row

parts.note: a row reads as a quarrel, but here it is rowing a boat; the woman pulls an oar

explanation.surface: A woman is caught up in an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes with 'cow' on the surface but is the boating 'row' in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A female rower in a crew is literally involved in rowing, a row on the water.

clue.text: Loathing having to be injected with drug, take a seat and dither

indicators.note: the word for loathing receives the other pieces inside it

parts.note: hate means loathing
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
to sit is to take a seat

explanation.surface: A hateful addict, after a fix, sits down and wavers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drug' gives E, slang for ecstasy; 'to be injected with' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither is to be indecisive, holding back from acting, a close synonym.

clue.text: Soldiers organise line in conflict

indicators.note: in conflict suggests the letters of organise and line are at war and scattered

explanation.surface: Troops arrange a line of battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organise' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'in conflict' is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a legion, such as the French Foreign Legion, are soldiers.

clue.text: Outside this place a theologian held fast

indicators.note: Outside places the theologian's letters around the word for this place

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian's degree
here means this place

explanation.surface: A theologian clung on outside this building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' sits before the pieces but wraps the theologian around this place, after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick, so having adhered is having clung or stuck firmly.

clue.text: River always descending between two points

indicators.note: between places the word for always inside the two compass points

parts.note: S and N are compass points, south and north
N is north, the second compass point
ever means always

explanation.surface: A river constantly flows downhill between two spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'descending' just reflects that in a down clue EVER lies between S and N.
explanation.definitionFit: The Severn is Britain's longest river, flowing from Wales into the Bristol Channel.

clue.text: Some believers getting back to America

parts.note: hind means back, as in hind legs
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: Some believers are returning to the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a direction but is the adjective HIND.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of Hinduism are religious adherents, a group of believers.

clue.text: Filth from birds finally landing on tree

indicators.note: in a down clue, landing on means placed on top of the following piece
finally takes the closing letter of the word birds

parts.note: the lime is a tree, also called a linden

explanation.surface: Bird droppings end up on a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Slime is mucky, sticky dirt, and so is a kind of filth.

clue.text: Gun — method it needs to get duck, but it's missing duck!

parts.note: how means the way or method

indicators.note: missing means the letter O drops out of the word for duck

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of zero
O resembles a zero, so it too is a duck

explanation.surface: A gunner needs a way to bag a duck, yet misses.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of nought, so it gives ZERO, and O. 'missing' strips O from ZERO.
explanation.definitionFit: A howitzer is a short artillery piece firing shells at high angles, a type of cannon.

clue.text: Number at that place a bit confused inside

indicators.note: a bit of the interior of the word for that place is jumbled, one letter shifting position

parts.note: there means at that place

explanation.surface: Someone over there is somewhat muddled within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit confused inside' rearranges the middle of THERE, moving R after H.
explanation.definitionFit: Three is a cardinal numeral, the integer after two.

clue.text: Arrogant one laughing in a London art gallery?

definitions.meaning: offhand and haughty, dismissive of others

definitions.text: one laughing in a London art gallery?
definitions.meaning: The Laughing ..., by Frans Hals, hangs in the Wallace Collection in London

explanation.walkthrough: The Wallace Collection is a London art museum.
explanation.definitionFit: Haughty disdain is the adjective's sense, and the Frans Hals portrait of a smiling royalist soldier gives the noun.

clue.text: Decided holy book needs editor

parts.note: Mark is the second Gospel, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A religious text needs an editor, it has been resolved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decided' is the adjective, as in a decided improvement.
explanation.definitionFit: A decided difference is a clear, noticeable one, just as a marked difference is.

clue.text: Old-fashioned officer, busy type grabbing naughty lad

indicators.note: grabbing has the word for busy type clutching the scrambled lad

parts.note: a busy bee is a crossword stand-in for a hard worker

indicators.note: naughty suggests the letters of lad misbehave and change places

explanation.surface: An official hurries to seize a misbehaving boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' scrambles lad into ADL, which 'grabbing' places within the busy type.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish officer who kept order in church and punished minor offenders, now a historical role.

clue.text: One's upset by muck in underground rooms

parts.note: dung is manure, muck

indicators.note: upset says the letters of One's are overturned and reordered

explanation.surface: Someone is distressed by the dirt in the cellars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles One's into EONS; 'One's' is not a possessive here.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungeons are dark cells beneath a castle, vaults below ground for prisoners.
